subject: Sable discovery — SDK/auth/reranker reliability follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@sableanalytics.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-19T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sable discovery — SDK/auth/reranker reliability follow-up

Hi Liam — great demo earlier, thanks for the time. Quick recap and a focused set of asks so we can scope a pilot that proves both function and reliability.

Recap (what we saw)
- You run a near-real-time search+rerank pipeline: chunking -> embeddings -> k-NN -> reranker model.
- Primary latency SLO: 300ms p95 for single-query rerank path for 2k daily active users during pilot.
- Data sensitivity: customer PII can appear in queries; must support eventual field-level redaction + KMS integration.

Open questions / asks for engineering scoping
1) SDK and auth: what languages does your ingestion layer prefer (JS/Python/Go)? Do you require mTLS or will token-based auth (rotating API keys + KMS) suffice for pilot?
2) Routing / traffic shaping: will you want us to route traffic to a dedicated pool for the pilot, or is multi-tenant hosted acceptable initially?
3) Structured output expectations: the reranker returns a JSON response with fields we should validate. Can you share a canonical JSON schema or an example response?
4) Failure & retry policy: what are acceptable retry windows (e.g., immediate retry x2 within 500ms, then fallback to cached result)?

Next steps proposed (mutual action plan)
- You: share a sample JSON output (1–2 examples) and procurement contact. Attach any RFP details.
- Us: produce an integration checklist and a constrained-decoding + validation approach aligned to your schema; propose retry patterns and an initial pilot config.
- Target: pilot readiness in 3 weeks if we align on schema and auth.

I attached an internal checklist template to show the level of detail we'll need. If you prefer, we can do a short follow-up 30-minute call to walk the schema.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0139

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@sableanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-19T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sable discovery — SDK/auth/reranker reliability follow-up

Thanks Marissa — really appreciate the clear recap. Attached is our RFP extract and a sample response payload from our reranker (redacted). Answers inline: 

- Languages: primary stack is Python (FastAPI) for inference, Node for frontend. Python SDK is preferred for a first pass.
- Auth: procurement will push for short-lived tokens backed by our KMS; mTLS is possible but heavier. We can start with token rotation + Vault/KMS.
- Routing: we'll accept a multi-tenant hosted pilot provided we can isolate traffic at the model/route level and have per-route SLAs. Dedicated pool is preferred for year-two.
- Retry: ideal behavior is: immediate retry x1 for transient 5xx, if still failing fall back to a cached top-1 result (stale <= 30s), then record a degradation event.

I attached Sable-RFP.pdf. Procurement is procurement@sableanalytics.com (cc'd on the procurement thread separately).

Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Search, Sable Analytics
liam.oconnor@sableanalytics.com

Subject: RE: Sable discovery — SDK/auth/reranker reliability follow-up (technical notes)

Putting a technical approach together based on Liam's answers. High-level proposal for the pilot: 

1) SDK & Auth
- Deliver a Python SDK (1.0) that supports: token rotation via KMS/Vault hooks, built-in retry helper, and native request batching.
- Auth modes: token-based by default; optional mTLS toggle in SDK config for Dedicated.

2) Structured output validation
- Request: ask Sable to provide a canonical JSON Schema. If they provide examples only, we will infer a strict schema and confirm.
- Constrained decoding approach: use token-level constraints + model-side stop sequences for known fields for the reranker (structured answer is mostly deterministic top-k + scores).
- Validation stage: post-generation validation against JSON Schema. If validation fails, two-tier fallback: 
  a) attempt constrained-regeneration (same prompt with narrower decoder constraints) up to 2 attempts;
  b) on continued failure, fall back to last-known-good cached response and emit a validation-failure telemetry event.

3) Retry patterns and latency tradeoffs
- For p95 300ms target: keep retry attempts lightweight. Immediate retry x1 (client-side) within 100–200ms window for transient network errors. Regeneration attempts that involve model decoding (constrained-regeneration) count as additional latency — those will be gated behind a 500ms budget per request during pilot.
- Observe: if regen increases tail latency too often, switch to cached-fallback-first for a percentage of requests (canary 5% traffic).

4) Routing & pilot infra
- Start with hosted multi-tenant routes with per-route isolation and capacity reservation. If we observe noisy neighbors, spin up a dedicated pool for Sable.

I'll draft these into the integration checklist and push a technical appendix to the Drive link.

— Dev

2) By Fri (3/23): Redwood to deliver: initial Python SDK draft + integration checklist + constrained-decoding appendix (includes cURL + Python snippets) and telemetry plan.
3) Week of 3/27: Pilot kickoff — pilot runs for 2 weeks with a 5% canary for regen-first attempts.

Files we uploaded to the Drive: integration checklist (internal_integration_checklist.xlsx), appendix (constrained-decoding.md). HubSpot deal is HB-3421.

If procurement wants an initial SOW or a pricing matrix for a dedicated pool, loop them into the thread and we'll prepare a one-pager.
